headline: Totals Went Oh For Three And The Model Called It Confidence
paragraphs: Twelve games got graded, six were left alone, and six of them coughed up nine tickets at ten dollars each. Two cashed. The week finished 2-7 for a loss of 54.46 dollars on 90 staked, an ROI of negative 60.5 percent, against a model that walked in announcing it expected to hit 67.1 percent. The gap between those two numbers is the whole column.

The totals market was the crime scene. Three plays, zero wins, thirty dollars gone, and the model rated that group at 75 percent. It took Over 39.5 at a stated 78 percent in South Florida at East Carolina, which ended 20-17, and it took Under 72 in a game Florida Atlantic won 60-29. One lonely bright spot: James Madison -13.5 in a 54-23 win, worth 9.09 dollars. The published top five went 0-2 at a 77.6 percent expectation.

Nine plays saw their line move and exactly one moved toward the model, which is 11.1 percent and roughly the market's opinion of the whole operation. Seven weeks graded for real now sit at 163-207-10 across 380 plays, down 482.16 dollars, an ROI of negative 12.7 percent, with a 44 percent win rate under a 60.5 percent expectation. The model is confident. The ledger is not.
